question.worked_solution:
We differentiate the given function with respect to $x,$ treating all other variables as constants. 

First, we use the product rule:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{x}(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}\operatorname{tan}⁡(x{y}^{2})) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2})\cdot \operatorname{tan}⁡(x{y}^{2})+{x}^{2}\cdot \frac{∂}{∂x}(\operatorname{tan}⁡(x{y}^{2}))\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we use the chain and the constant multiple rules:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2})\cdot \operatorname{tan}⁡(x{y}^{2})+{x}^{2}\cdot \frac{∂}{∂x}(\operatorname{tan}⁡(x{y}^{2})) & =(2x)\cdot \operatorname{tan}⁡(x{y}^{2})+{x}^{2}\cdot {sec}^{2}⁡(x{y}^{2})\frac{∂}{∂x}(x{y}^{2}) \\  & =2x\operatorname{tan}⁡(x{y}^{2})+{x}^{2}{sec}^{2}⁡(x{y}^{2})\cdot {y}^{2}\cdot \frac{∂}{∂x}(x) \\  & =2x\operatorname{tan}⁡(x{y}^{2})+{x}^{2}{sec}^{2}⁡(x{y}^{2})\cdot {y}^{2}\cdot (1) \\  & =2x\operatorname{tan}⁡(x{y}^{2})+{x}^{2}{y}^{2}{sec}^{2}⁡(x{y}^{2})\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the partial derivative at the point $(\frac{\pi }{4},1):$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x}{|}_{(\pi /4,1)} & =2\cdot \frac{\pi }{4}\cdot \operatorname{tan}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4}\cdot {1}^{2})+{(\frac{\pi }{4})}^{2}\cdot {1}^{2}\cdot {sec}^{2}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4}\cdot {1}^{2}) \\  & =2\cdot \frac{\pi }{4}\cdot 1+\frac{{\pi }^{2}}{16}\cdot (\sqrt{2})^{2} \\  & =\frac{\pi }{2}+\frac{{\pi }^{2}}{8} \\  & =\frac{{\pi }^{2}+4\pi }{8}\end{aligned}
$$
